## `osascript -e` 簡介

`osascript` 是 macOS 內建的 AppleScript / JavaScript for Automation 直譯器。`-e` 是 inline 跑一行腳本，不用先寫 `.scpt` 檔。

### 跟 app 互動的常見動詞

```bash
osascript -e 'quit app "OrbStack"'                       # 短語法，graceful 退出
osascript -e 'tell application "OrbStack" to quit'       # 等價，完整語法
osascript -e 'tell application "OrbStack" to activate'   # 啟動 + 帶到前景
osascript -e 'tell application "OrbStack" to launch'     # 啟動但不搶焦點（背景）
osascript -e 'tell application "OrbStack" to reopen'     # 已開就帶到前景，沒開就開
osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to set visible of process "OrbStack" to false'  # 隱藏
```

### 為什麼用 `osascript` 而不是 `killall` / `open`

| 方式 | 語意 | OrbStack 場景 |
|---|---|---|
| `osascript -e 'quit app "X"'` | 送 `Quit` Apple Event，等同你按 ⌘Q | **會等 container/VM 乾淨關閉** |
| `killall OrbStack` | SIGTERM（無 handler 就直接砍） | **可能留下 dangling state** |
| `kill -9 …` | SIGKILL 不可被攔截 | 救命用，平時別碰 |
| `open -a OrbStack` | 啟動 + 帶到前景 | 跟 `activate` 差在 `open` 不需要 app 已在執行 |
| `open -ga OrbStack` | 啟動但**不**搶焦點 | 跟 `launch` 語意接近，但更可靠 |

對 OrbStack/Docker Desktop 這種有 VM/daemon 的 app 來說，**永遠優先用 `quit`，不要 `killall`**。

### 進階：判斷 app 是否在跑

```bash
# 0 = 正在跑, 1 = 沒跑
osascript -e 'application "OrbStack" is running' | grep -q true && echo on || echo off

# 列出所有正在跑的 GUI app
osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every application process whose background only is false'
```

## 能做什麼 alias？

我看了 repo，目前 `dot_config/shell/` 沒有 macOS app 控制相關 helper。可以加一個 `dot_config/shell/55_macos_apps.sh`（POSIX、兩個 shell 都源、但用 `case "$(uname -s)" in Darwin) … esac` gate 起來），提供：

```sh
# 通用 helper
appquit()    { osascript -e "tell application \"$1\" to quit"; }
applaunch()  { osascript -e "tell application \"$1\" to launch"; }      # 背景啟動
appactivate(){ osascript -e "tell application \"$1\" to activate"; }    # 前景啟動
apprestart() { appquit "$1" && sleep 1 && applaunch "$1"; }
apprunning() { osascript -e "application \"$1\" is running" | grep -q true; }
```

然後對你常用的 app 做語意化 alias，例如：

```sh
alias orb-quit='appquit OrbStack'
alias orb-start='applaunch OrbStack'         # 背景啟動，不搶焦點
alias orb-restart='apprestart OrbStack'
```

```text
1	{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
2	# shellcheck shell=sh
3	# mac-mem-* helpers — diagnose + reclaim macOS memory / swap / storage
4	# pressure without rebooting.
5	#
6	# POSIX-portable wrappers around vm_stat / sysctl / footprint(1) /
7	# memory_pressure(1) / tmutil / pmset / sudo purge. Sourced by both bash
8	# and zsh via load_modular_dir of ~/.config/shell/. Darwin-only — the
9	# entire file is gated by the chezmoi `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` template
10	# so it never lands on Linux hosts. The defensive runtime check inside
11	# each function exists for the copy-paste-onto-Linux case.
12	#
13	# Why these helpers exist:
14	#   - macOS dynamically grows /private/var/vm/swapfile* up to free disk
15	#     and only contracts them on reboot. "System Data" / "Other Volumes"
16	#     in About > Storage balloons silently.
17	#   - Activity Monitor's Memory Pressure graph going green/yellow does
18	#     NOT mean swap shrunk — it usually didn't.
19	#   - `ps -o rss` cannot see compressed or swapped pages on Apple
20	#     Silicon; `footprint(1)` can.
21	#
22	# See: docs/tools/macos-swap.md (full deep-dive incl. why reboot really
23	# is the answer sometimes), docs/shells/aliases.md (one-line summary
24	# row per function), pitfalls/macos-swap-files-never-shrink.md.
25	#
26	# Conventions (mirror dot_config/shell/45_audit.sh.tmpl):
27	#   - All public functions accept --help.
28	#   - Sudo path: interactive TTY -> single `sudo -v` then sudo <cmd>;
29	#     non-interactive -> exit 1 with stderr hint. Does NOT integrate
30	#     with scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh (that helper is run-script-scoped
31	#     and not deployed to ~/).
32	#   - All functions exit 0 on broken pipe (head | less etc.).
33	#   - Color output via tput when stdout is a TTY; bare otherwise.
34	
35	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
36	# Internal helpers (prefix _macmem_ — not part of public surface)
37	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
38	
39	_macmem_is_darwin() { [ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" = "Darwin" ]; }
40	_macmem_is_tty() { [ -t 1 ]; }
41	_macmem_is_arm64() { [ "$(uname -m 2>/dev/null)" = "arm64" ]; }
42	_macmem_have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
43	
44	_macmem_guard_darwin() {
45	    if ! _macmem_is_darwin; then
46	        printf 'mac-mem: this helper is macOS-only (current OS: %s)\n' \
47	            "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" >&2
48	        return 1
49	    fi
50	}
51	
52	# Run "$@" with sudo if not root. If sudo would prompt and we're
53	# non-interactive, fail with hint.
54	_macmem_run_root() {
55	    if [ "$(id -u)" = "0" ]; then
56	        "$@"
57	        return $?
58	    fi
59	    if ! _macmem_have sudo; then
60	        printf 'mac-mem: needs root and sudo not installed\n' >&2
```

```tmpl
{{- if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
# shellcheck shell=sh
# app-* helpers — graceful control of macOS GUI apps via osascript / Apple Events.
#
# Why not `killall`? `killall AppName` sends SIGTERM and most GUI apps don't
# register a handler, so containers / unsaved buffers / background sync just
# die. `osascript -e 'tell application "X" to quit'` sends the Quit Apple
# Event — the same thing ⌘Q does — so the app tears down cleanly. Matters
# for OrbStack / Docker Desktop / Slack / any app with state.
#
# Frozen-app detection (`appresponsive`) is best-effort: macOS exposes the
# "Not Responding" flag only via Activity Monitor's private SPI. The public
# proxy is "send a no-op Apple Event with a short timeout — if it throws,
# the app is hung." False positives happen on apps mid-launch.
#
# All helpers take an app NAME (e.g. `OrbStack`, `Google Chrome`), not a
# bundle ID. `$1` is passed via osascript's `argv` so spaces and quotes in
# app names are handled correctly without shell-escaping gymnastics.

_macapp_is_darwin() { [ "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null)" = "Darwin" ]; }

_macapp_guard_darwin() {
    if ! _macapp_is_darwin; then
        printf 'app-helper: macOS-only (current OS: %s)\n' \
            "$(uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

_macapp_need_name() {
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
        printf 'usage: %s <AppName>\n  e.g. %s OrbStack\n' "$2" "$2" >&2
        return 2
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public: lifecycle
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# appquit NAME — send Quit Apple Event (graceful, equivalent to ⌘Q).
appquit() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: appquit <AppName>\n  Send Quit Apple Event (graceful shutdown).\n  Example: appquit OrbStack\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
    _macapp_need_name "$1" appquit || return 2
    osascript \
        -e 'on run argv' \
        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to quit' \
        -e 'end run' \
        -- "$1"
}

# applaunch NAME — start the app in the background (no focus steal).
applaunch() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: applaunch <AppName>\n  Launch in background (no focus steal). Use appactivate to bring to front.\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
    _macapp_need_name "$1" applaunch || return 2
    osascript \
        -e 'on run argv' \
        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to launch' \
        -e 'end run' \
        -- "$1"
}

# appactivate NAME — start (if needed) and bring to front.
appactivate() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: appactivate <AppName>\n  Launch + bring to front. Use applaunch for headless start.\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
    _macapp_need_name "$1" appactivate || return 2
    osascript \
        -e 'on run argv' \
        -e 'tell application (item 1 of argv) to activate' \
        -e 'end run' \
        -- "$1"
}

# apprestart NAME — quit, wait for shutdown, relaunch in background.
apprestart() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: apprestart <AppName>\n  Graceful quit + background relaunch. Useful after config edits.\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
    _macapp_need_name "$1" apprestart || return 2
    appquit "$1" || return $?
    # Poll until really gone — `quit` returns before the app process exits.
    _macapp_i=0
    while [ "$_macapp_i" -lt 30 ] && apprunning "$1"; do
        sleep 0.5
        _macapp_i=$((_macapp_i + 1))
    done
    unset _macapp_i
    applaunch "$1"
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public: inspection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# apprunning NAME — exit 0 if app is running, 1 otherwise. Silent.
apprunning() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: apprunning <AppName>\n  Exit 0 if running, 1 otherwise. Silent — use $? or && / ||.\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
    _macapp_need_name "$1" apprunning || return 2
    _macapp_out=$(osascript \
        -e 'on run argv' \
        -e 'tell application "System Events" to return (exists (processes where name is (item 1 of argv)))' \
        -e 'end run' \
        -- "$1" 2>/dev/null)
    [ "$_macapp_out" = "true" ]
}

# applist [--pids] — list visible (foreground) GUI apps, one per line.
# Default: just names. `--pids` adds PID + bundle path.
applist() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: applist [--pids|--all]\n'
        printf '  Default     names of visible foreground GUI apps, one per line.\n'
        printf '  --pids      "<pid>\\t<name>" via lsappinfo (foreground only).\n'
        printf '  --all       include background-only / agent processes.\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1

    case "${1:-}" in
        --pids)
            # lsappinfo is a public macOS CLI; output is pid + bundle path lines.
            command -v lsappinfo >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
                printf 'applist --pids: needs lsappinfo (macOS built-in)\n' >&2
                return 1
            }
            lsappinfo list 2>/dev/null \
                | awk '
                    /^[0-9]+\)/ {
                        pid=""; name="";
                        match($0, /pid = [0-9]+/);
                        if (RSTART) pid=substr($0, RSTART+6, RLENGTH-6);
                        match($0, /"[^"]+"/);
                        if (RSTART) name=substr($0, RSTART+1, RLENGTH-2);
                        if (pid != "" && name != "") printf "%s\t%s\n", pid, name;
                    }'
            ;;
        --all)
            osascript \
                -e 'tell application "System Events" to set procNames to name of every process' \
                -e 'set AppleScript'\''s text item delimiters to linefeed' \
                -e 'return procNames as text'
            ;;
        ""|*)
            osascript \
                -e 'tell application "System Events" to set procNames to name of every application process whose background only is false' \
                -e 'set AppleScript'\''s text item delimiters to linefeed' \
                -e 'return procNames as text'
            ;;
    esac
}

# appresponsive NAME [TIMEOUT_SEC] — exit 0 if app responds within timeout.
# Sends a no-op Get-name Apple Event with `with timeout`. If AppleScript
# throws (timeout or "isn't running"), exit 1.
#
# Best-effort: this is the public-API proxy for "Not Responding". An app
# mid-launch may falsely fail; raise TIMEOUT (default 2s) to reduce noise.
appresponsive() {
    case "$1" in -h|--help)
        printf 'usage: appresponsive <AppName> [TIMEOUT_SEC]\n'
        printf '  Exit 0 if app answers an Apple Event within TIMEOUT (default 2s).\n'
        printf '  Exit 1 if hung, not running, or scripting-disabled.\n'
        printf '  Example: appresponsive OrbStack 5 || echo hung\n'
        return 0 ;;
    esac
    _macapp_guard_darwin || return 1
    _macapp_need_name "$1" appresponsive || return 2
    _macapp_to=${2:-2}
    apprunning "$1" || return 1
    _macapp_out=$(osascript \
        -e 'on run argv' \
        -e 'set t to (item 2 of argv) as integer' \
        -e 'with timeout of t seconds' \
        -e '  try' \
        -e '    tell application (item 1 of argv) to get name' \
        -e '    return "yes"' \
        -e '  on error' \
        -e '    return "no"' \
        -e '  end try' \
        -e 'end timeout' \
        -e 'end run' \
        -- "$1" "$_macapp_to" 2>/dev/null)
    unset _macapp_to
    [ "$_macapp_out" = "yes" ]
}

{{ end -}}
```
